{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjccM8AAAABZea-fQ", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3IfzhDFoR4", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3If", "number": 43, "title": "Correct V30MZ MUL/IMUL flags across all three WonderSwan models", "body": "## Problem

At baseline `d21e16af634bb3e6c73ab08b111a2bcc51fae465`, `crates/ws-core/src/cpu.rs:785` and `:970` update only CF/OF after multiplication, retaining AF/PF/SF/ZF. Independent WonderSwan CPU experiments report deterministic values instead. This can change subsequent conditional control flow on WonderSwan, WonderSwan Color and SwanCrystal. Commercial-title impact remains unmeasured.

For example, `F6 E3` with AL=3, BL=2 and incoming FLAGS=`F002` currently produces FLAGS=`F002` everywhere; Color/Crystal should produce `F042`.

## Expected outcome

Correct ordinary multiplication execution for unsigned `F6/F7 /4`, signed `F6/F7 /5`, and immediate signed `69/6B`:

- Clear AF/PF/SF.
- Unsigned MUL: clear ZF on physical WonderSwan; set ZF on physical Color/Crystal, independently of active graphics mode.
- Signed IMUL, including both immediate forms: set ZF on every model.
- Preserve correct products, destinations and CF/OF fit/overflow rules, unrelated control flags, decoding, bus accounting and shared-clock scheduling.

## Context

The clean checkout and inspected remote main match the baseline. Open Issues/PRs are empty; closed history contains no equivalent completed flag correction. Earlier arithmetic work and Issues #35, #39 and #41 remain regression obligations.

The [NEC V30MZ manual](https://www.renesas.com/en/document/lbr/v30mztm-hardware-preliminary), §3.1.5, leaves several multiplication flags undefined. That does not establish preservation. The inspected [WSCPUTest report](https://github.com/FluBBaOfWard/WSCPUTest/blob/245b12c06dede4a2bb9c04c942ebca2044ba4930/README.md) supplies the console-specific rules above. Its [assembly](https://github.com/FluBBaOfWard/WSCPUTest/blob/245b12c06dede4a2bb9c04c942ebca2044ba4930/WSCpuTest.asm) selects unsigned flags using physical-model identification at lines 64–70 and compares products/full flags under contrasting incoming flags from line 4346. Immediate-word and sign-extended-byte IMUL tests begin at lines 4832 and 4953.

Correction record: replace the current implicit assumption that undefined multiplication flags remain unchanged with the reported deterministic rules. Also correct the latest assessment's unresolved immediate-IMUL prerequisite: the inspected source covers both forms. Record this evidence and rationale without weakening prior acceptance. The report/source is an independent hardware experiment reference; no physical execution or per-model measurement log was independently inspected.

Existing multiplication tests check products and CF/OF, without full-flag/model assertions. [Saved #41 validation](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/d21e16af634bb3e6c73ab08b111a2bcc51fae465/docs/issue-41-validation.md) reports 121 core tests, 18 integration tests, one adapter test and both complete Chromium suites passing. These are Coordinator-reported results, not planning-time reruns. Division quirks, other arithmetic, single-step delivery and absolute instruction timing remain separate gaps.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Record the source reconciliation, both corrected assumptions, physical-model applicability and experimental limits. Implement every multiplication form listed above through normal decoding; introduce no game-specific behavior or generic fallback.
- [ ] Add independent full-FLAGS/product vectors with contrasting incoming arithmetic and control flags. Cover zero/nonzero products, positive/negative operands, signed fit boundaries and overflow, byte/word forms, both immediate widths and `6B` sign extension. Check untouched registers and immediate destination/source aliasing.
- [ ] Exercise all five model/mode combinations: Mono, Color in mono/color modes, and Crystal in mono/color modes. Include runtime mode transitions proving unsigned ZF follows physical hardware. Demonstrate baseline failures for unsigned, signed and immediate paths before fixing production code.
- [ ] Cover register and mapped-memory sources, aligned/odd word operands and segment overrides. Preserve instruction length, operand access accounting, execution-cost components and advancement of shared devices exactly once. Retain existing prefix, interrupt-shadow, HALT, REP, BUSLOCK and FPO1/POLL assertions; do not fold timing redesign into this change.
- [ ] Add an original source-included CC0 probe covering all multiplication forms and applicable modes. Verify actual CPU-written products/full flags and subsequent conditional branches natively and through the production Chromium/Wasm player on all three models and restart. Clear completion state and require fresh boot/completion markers so retained saves cannot manufacture a pass; record baseline discrimination and corrected results.
- [ ] Preserve three-model gates, firmware-free handoff, LCD behavior, audio/PCM, GDMA/SDMA/Hyper Voice, SRAM, cartridge/internal EEPROM, browser save integrity, input/frame continuity and ownership/provenance. Retain unrelated acceptance assertions and existing fixture/demo bytes.
- [ ] Before merge, Coordinator runs and records `python3 fixtures/build.py --check`, `python3 demo/build.py --check`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo test --workspace --locked`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `git diff --check`. In `web`, run `npm run build:wasm`, `npm run build`, then complete `npm run test:browser` and `npm run test:compat` sequentially against that production build, including the new probe.
- [ ] Update hardware-support documentation, fixture provenance and validation evidence. Coordinator reviews the final diff against every checkbox before merge, resolves blocking findings and distinguishes tests present from checks actually executed, including failures and unperformed optional checks.

## Optional validation

Expand operand coverage with independent reference calculations or compare the original probe with lawfully available physical-console observations. No proprietary ROM/firmware or human gameplay is required. Probe success establishes bounded hardware behavior, not commercial-catalog compatibility.

## Required post-merge verification

None.

## Specification reconciliation

This task was authored by AI under the agreed WonderSwan-family hardware goal.
Correct erroneous technical assumptions or acceptance criteria when primary hardware
specifications establish the correction. Update this Issue and record the original
assumption, corrected requirement, primary reference and rationale in the PR.
These technical corrections require neither human approval nor an independent AI
re-review. Preserve the agreed goal and relevant pre-merge acceptance; do not weaken
requirements merely to accommodate incomplete implementation or failing tests.
